name: apply_patch
description:
Use the `apply_patch` tool to edit files.
Your patch language is a stripped-down, file-oriented diff format designed to be easy to parse and safe to apply. You can think of it as a high-level envelope:

*** Begin Patch
[ one or more file sections ]
*** End Patch

Within that envelope, you get a sequence of file operations.
You MUST include a header to specify the action you are taking.
Each operation starts with one of three headers:

*** Add File: <path> - create a new file. Every following line is a + line (the initial contents).
*** Delete File: <path> - remove an existing file. Nothing follows.
*** Update File: <path> - patch an existing file in place (optionally with a rename).

May be immediately followed by *** Move to: <new path> if you want to rename the file.
Then one or more “hunks”, each introduced by @@ (optionally followed by a hunk header).
Within a hunk each line starts with:

For instructions on [context_before] and [context_after]:
- By default, show 3 lines of code immediately above and 3 lines immediately below each change. If a change is within 3 lines of a previous change, do NOT duplicate the first change's [context_after] lines in the second change's [context_before] lines.
- If 3 lines of context is insufficient to uniquely identify the snippet of code within the file, use the @@ operator to indicate the class or function to which the snippet belongs. For instance, we might have:
@@ class BaseClass
[3 lines of pre-context]
- [old_code]
+ [new_code]
[3 lines of post-context]

- If a code block is repeated so many times in a class or function such that even a single `@@` statement and 3 lines of context cannot uniquely identify the snippet of code, you can use multiple `@@` statements to jump to the right context. For instance:

@@ class BaseClass
@@ 	 def method():
[3 lines of pre-context]
- [old_code]
+ [new_code]
[3 lines of post-context]

The full grammar definition is below:
Patch := Begin { FileOp } End
Begin := "*** Begin Patch" NEWLINE
End := "*** End Patch" NEWLINE
FileOp := AddFile | DeleteFile | UpdateFile
AddFile := "*** Add File: " path NEWLINE { "+" line NEWLINE }
DeleteFile := "*** Delete File: " path NEWLINE
UpdateFile := "*** Update File: " path NEWLINE [ MoveTo ] { Hunk }
MoveTo := "*** Move to: " newPath NEWLINE
Hunk := "@@" [ header ] NEWLINE { HunkLine } [ "*** End of File" NEWLINE ]
HunkLine := (" " | "-" | "+") text NEWLINE

A full patch can combine several operations:

*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: hello.txt
+Hello world
*** Update File: src/app.py
*** Move to: src/main.py
@@ def greet():
-print("Hi")
+print("Hello, world!")
*** Delete File: obsolete.txt
*** End Patch

It is important to remember:

- You must include a header with your intended action (Add/Delete/Update)
- You must prefix new lines with `+` even when creating a new file
- File references must be ABSOLUTE, NEVER RELATIVE.

name: create_directory
description: Create a new directory structure in the workspace. Will recursively create all directories in the path, like mkdir -p. You do not need to use this tool before using create_file, that tool will automatically create the needed directories.

name: create_file
description: This is a tool for creating a new file in the workspace. The file will be created with the specified content. The directory will be created if it does not already exist. Never use this tool to edit a file that already exists.

name: file_search
description:
Search for files in the workspace by glob pattern. This only returns the paths of matching files. Use this tool when you know the exact filename pattern of the files you're searching for. Glob patterns match from the root of the workspace folder. Examples:
- **/*.{js,ts} to match all js/ts files in the workspace.
- src/** to match all files under the top-level src folder.
- **/foo/**/*.js to match all js files under any foo folder in the workspace.

In a multi-root workspace, you can scope the search to a specific workspace folder by using the absolute path to the folder as the query, e.g. /path/to/folder/**/*.ts.

name: grep_search
description:
Do a fast text search in the workspace. Use this tool when you want to search with an exact string or regex. If you are not sure what words will appear in the workspace, prefer using regex patterns with alternation (|) or character classes to search for multiple potential words at once instead of making separate searches. For example, use 'function|method|procedure' to look for all of those words at once. Use includePattern to search within files matching a specific pattern, or in a specific file, using a relative path. Use 'includeIgnoredFiles' to include files normally ignored by .gitignore, other ignore files, and `files.exclude` and `search.exclude` settings. Warning: using this may cause the search to be slower, only set it when you want to search in ignored folders like node_modules or build outputs. Use this tool when you want to see an overview of a particular file, instead of using read_file many times to look for code within a file.

In a multi-root workspace, you can scope the search to a specific workspace folder by using the absolute path to the folder as the includePattern, e.g. /path/to/folder.

name: list_dir
description: List the contents of a directory. Result will have the name of the child. If the name ends in /, it's a folder, otherwise a file

name: read_file
description:
Read the contents of a file.

You must specify the line range you're interested in. Line numbers are 1-indexed. If the file contents returned are insufficient for your task, you may call this tool again to retrieve more content. Prefer reading larger ranges over doing many small reads. Binary files use startLine/endLine as byte offsets.

name: resolve_memory_file_uri
description: Resolve a memory file path (like /memories/session/plan.md or /memories/repo/notes.md) to its fully qualified URI. Use this when you need the actual URI for a memory file, for example to pass it to setArtifacts. The path must start with /memories/.

name: semantic_search
description: Run a natural language search for relevant code or documentation comments from the user's current workspace. Returns relevant code snippets from the user's current workspace if it is large, or the full contents of the workspace if it is small.

name: view_image
description: View the contents of an image file. Use this instead of read_file for supported image files such as png, jpg, jpeg, gif, and webp. The tool returns the image directly to multimodal models and does not take line ranges or offsets.

name: execution_subagent
description:
Launch an iterative execution-focused subagent that performs an execution-based task.
USE THIS INSTEAD OF RUNNING INDIVIDUAL COMMANDS WITH run_in_terminal EXCEPT IN THE RARE CASES THAT YOU NEED THE FULL OUTPUT OF A COMMAND.
Here are some examples of how it can be used:
- Run tests and filter the output to summarize which tests failed and why.
- Install all dependencies of a project.
Returns: A list of commands that were run, along with relevant excerpts of each command's output.
Input fields:
- query: What to execute, and what to look for in the output. Can include exact commands to run, or a description of an execution task.
- description: Short user-visible invocation message.
NOTE: In the subagent query, make sure to specify any restrictions or guidelines on running commands provided by the user earlier in the conversation.
For example, if the user instructs the agent to not edit files in a particular directory, make sure to include that instruction in the subagent query when relevant.

name: get_terminal_output
description: Get output from a terminal session. This can target either a persistent terminal started with run_in_terminal in async mode (using 'id') or any foreground terminal visible in the terminal panel (using 'terminalId'). For the 'id' parameter, this must be the exact opaque UUID returned by run_in_terminal; terminal names, labels, and integers are not valid for 'id'.

name: manage_todo_list
description:
Updates the task plan.
Provide an optional explanation and a list of plan items, each with a step and status.
At most one step can be in_progress at a time.

name: run_in_terminal
description:
This tool allows you to execute shell commands in a persistent zsh terminal session, preserving environment variables, working directory, and other context across multiple commands.

Command Execution:
- Use && to chain simple commands on one line
- Prefer pipelines | over temporary files for data flow
- Never create a sub-shell (eg. bash -c "command") unless explicitly asked

Directory Management:
- Prefer relative paths when navigating directories, only use absolute when the path is far away or the current cwd is not expected
- By default (mode=sync), shell and cwd are reused by subsequent sync commands
- Use $PWD for current directory references
- Consider using pushd/popd for directory stack management
- Supports directory shortcuts like ~ and -

Program Execution:
- Supports Python, Node.js, and other executables
- Install packages via package managers (brew, apt, etc.)
- Use which or command -v to verify command availability

Async Mode:
- For long-running tasks (e.g., servers), use mode=async
- Returns a terminal ID for checking status and runtime later

Use send_to_terminal to send commands or input to a terminal session.

Output Management:
- Output is automatically truncated if longer than 60KB to prevent context overflow
- Use head, tail, grep, awk to filter and limit output size
- For pager commands, disable paging: git --no-pager or add | cat
- Use wc -l to count lines before displaying large outputs

Best Practices:
- Quote variables: "$var" instead of $var to handle spaces
- Use find with -exec or xargs for file operations
- Be specific with commands to avoid excessive output
- Avoid printing credentials unless absolutely required
- NEVER run sleep or similar wait commands in a terminal. You will be automatically notified on your next turn when async terminal commands or timed-out sync commands complete or need input. Use get_terminal_output to check output before then

Interactive Input Handling:
- When a terminal command is waiting for interactive input, do NOT suggest alternatives or ask the user whether to proceed. Instead, use the vscode_askQuestions tool to collect the needed values from the user, then send them.
- Send exactly one answer per prompt using send_to_terminal. Never send multiple answers in a single send.
- After each send, call get_terminal_output to read the next prompt before sending the next answer.
- Continue one prompt at a time until the command finishes.
- Use type to check command type (builtin, function, alias)
- Use jobs, fg, bg for job control
- Use [[ ]] for conditional tests instead of [ ]
- Prefer $() over backticks for command substitution
- Use setopt errexit for strict error handling
- Take advantage of zsh globbing features (**, extended globs)

Execution mode:
- mode='sync': wait for completion up to timeout; if still running, return with a terminal ID.
- mode='async': wait for an initial idle/output signal, then return with terminal output snapshot and ID. Timeout caps how long to wait for the initial idle/output signal.
- Prefer mode='sync' for commands that will prompt for interactive input (e.g., npm init, interactive installers, configuration wizards).

Terminal notifications: When an async command finishes or a sync command times out, you will be automatically notified on your next turn with the exit code and terminal output. You will also be notified if the terminal needs input. Use get_terminal_output to check output before then. Do NOT poll or sleep to wait for completion.

name: runSubagent
description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks autonomously. This tool is good at researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries, use this agent to perform the search for you.

- Agents do not run async or in the background, you will wait for the agent's result.
- When the agent is done, it will return a single message back to you. The result returned by the agent is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result.
- Each agent invocation is stateless. You will not be able to send additional messages to the agent, nor will the agent be able to communicate with you outside of its final report. Therefore, your prompt should contain a highly detailed task description for the agent to perform autonomously and you should specify exactly what information the agent should return back to you in its final and only message to you.
- The agent's outputs should generally be trusted
- Clearly tell the agent whether you expect it to write code or just to do research (search, file reads, web fetches, etc.), since it is not aware of the user's intent
- If the user asks for a certain agent, you MUST provide that EXACT agent name (case-sensitive) to invoke that specific agent.

name: search_subagent
description:
Launch a fast agent specialized for exploring codebases. Use this when you need to quickly find files by patterns (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), search code for keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer questions about the codebase (eg. "how do API endpoints work?").
Returns: A list of relevant files/snippet locations in the workspace.

Input fields:
- query: Natural language description of what to search for.
- description: Short user-visible invocation message. 
- details: 2-3 sentences detailing the objective of the search agent.

name: vscode_listCodeUsages
description:
Find all usages (references, definitions, and implementations) of a code symbol across the workspace. This tool locates where a symbol is referenced, defined, or implemented.

Input:
- "symbol": The exact name of the symbol to search for (function, class, method, variable, type, etc.).
- "uri": A full URI (e.g. "file:///path/to/file.ts") of a file where the symbol appears. Provide either "uri" or "filePath".
- "filePath": A workspace-relative file path (e.g. "src/utils/helpers.ts") of a file where the symbol appears. Provide either "uri" or "filePath".
- "lineContent": A substring of the line of code where the symbol appears. This is used to locate the exact position in the file. Must be the actual text from the file - do NOT fabricate it.

IMPORTANT: The file and line do NOT need to be the definition of the symbol. Any occurrence works - a usage, an import, a call site, etc. You can pick whichever occurrence is most convenient.

If the tool returns an error, retry with corrected input - ensure the file path is correct, the line content matches the actual file content, and the symbol name appears in that line.

Currently supported for: chatagent, instructions, json, markdown, prompt, skill.

name: vscode_renameSymbol
description:
Rename a code symbol across the workspace using the language server's rename functionality. This performs a precise, semantics-aware rename that updates all references.

Input:
- "symbol": The exact current name of the symbol to rename.
- "newName": The new name for the symbol.
- "uri": A full URI (e.g. "file:///path/to/file.ts") of a file where the symbol appears. Provide either "uri" or "filePath".
- "filePath": A workspace-relative file path (e.g. "src/utils/helpers.ts") of a file where the symbol appears. Provide either "uri" or "filePath".
- "lineContent": A substring of the line of code where the symbol appears. This is used to locate the exact position in the file. Must be the actual text from the file - do NOT fabricate it.

IMPORTANT: The file and line do NOT need to be the definition of the symbol. Any occurrence works - a usage, an import, a call site, etc. You can pick whichever occurrence is most convenient.

If the tool returns an error, retry with corrected input - ensure the file path is correct, the line content matches the actual file content, and the symbol name appears in that line.

Currently supported for: chatagent, instructions, markdown, prompt, skill.

name: vscode_searchExtensions_internal
description: This is a tool for browsing Visual Studio Code Extensions Marketplace. It allows the model to search for extensions and retrieve detailed information about them. The model should use this tool whenever it needs to discover extensions or resolve information about known ones. To use the tool, the model has to provide the category of the extensions, relevant search keywords, or known extension IDs. Note that search results may include false positives, so reviewing and filtering is recommended.

name: kill_terminal
description: Kill a terminal by its ID. Use this to clean up terminals that are no longer needed (e.g., after stopping a server or when a long-running task completes). The terminal ID is returned by run_in_terminal in async mode (legacy: isBackground=true).

name: send_to_terminal
description: Send input text to a terminal session. This can target either a persistent terminal started with run_in_terminal in async mode (using 'id') or any foreground terminal visible in the terminal panel (using 'terminalId'). The 'command' field may be empty or whitespace to press Enter (useful for interactive prompts). After sending, use get_terminal_output to check updated output for persistent terminals.

name: task_complete
description:
Signal that the user's task is fully done. You MUST call this tool when your work is complete — whether you made code changes, answered a question, or completed any other kind of task. Provide a brief summary of what was accomplished. Do not restate the summary in your message text — it is shown to the user directly.

IMPORTANT: Before calling this tool, you MUST output a brief text message summarizing what was done. The task is not complete until both your summary message AND this tool call are present.

When to call:
- After answering the user's question or completing a conversational request
- After you have completed ALL requested changes
- After verifying results: tests pass, terminal commands succeeded, tool calls returned expected output

When NOT to call:
- If a terminal command failed or produced unexpected output
- If an MCP or external tool call returned an error
- If you encountered errors you have not resolved
- If there are remaining steps to complete
- If you have not verified your changes work

This group focuses on tools that assist in upgrading .NET projects, providing a comprehensive suite for assessing upgrade scenarios and generating necessary assessments. The 'discover_upgrade_scenarios' tool identifies potential upgrade paths, while 'generate_dotnet_upgrade_assessment' produces a detailed analysis of a project's readiness for upgrade, highlighting issues, breaking changes, and compatibility risks. The 'get_dotnet_upgrade_options' tool provides information on available upgrade options, including target frameworks and proposed versions. Additionally, 'initialize_scenario' sets up the necessary structure for a modernization scenario, and 'query_dotnet_assessment' allows users to delve into specific assessment details. Collectively, these tools streamline the upgrade process, ensuring that developers have the insights needed to navigate complex migrations.

Be sure to call this tool if you need a capability related to the above.

This group of tools is dedicated to analyzing dependencies within .NET projects, providing insights into code relationships and potential migration paths. The 'get_code_dependencies' tool constructs a dependency graph for specific C# classes or views, helping developers understand what components need to be migrated together. The 'get_member_info' and 'get_namespace_info' tools offer detailed information about type members and namespaces, respectively, including potential breaking changes and updates. Additionally, 'get_project_dependencies' provides a comprehensive list of all dependencies for a project, while 'get_projects_in_topological_order' helps visualize project dependencies in a structured manner. Together, these tools empower developers to make informed decisions during the migration process by clarifying how different parts of the codebase interact.

Be sure to call this tool if you need a capability related to the above.

name: activate_workflow_state_management_tools

The 'get_state' tool retrieves the current status of the task workflow, providing insights into the scenario status, current tasks, and task hierarchy. This is essential for understanding where the workflow stands at any given moment. The 'resume_scenario' tool allows users to continue working on an existing scenario that has been previously saved, ensuring that no progress is lost and that users can pick up right where they left off. Together, these tools enhance workflow management by providing visibility and continuity, allowing teams to maintain focus and efficiency in their projects.

Be sure to call this tool if you need a capability related to the above.

This group of tools is focused on validating the .NET SDK environment to ensure compatibility with project upgrades. The 'validate_dotnet_sdk_in_globaljson' tool checks that the specified .NET SDK version in the global.json file aligns with the required version for an upgrade, preventing potential issues during the migration process. Meanwhile, 'validate_dotnet_sdk_installation' verifies that the necessary .NET SDK version is installed on the machine, ensuring that developers have the correct tools available for their projects. Together, these tools provide a safety net for developers, helping to avoid common pitfalls associated with SDK version mismatches and ensuring a smoother upgrade experience.

Be sure to call this tool if you need a capability related to the above.

name: mcp_copilotmod_authenticate_nuget_feed
description:
Call authenticate_nuget_feed to resolve NuGet package authentication failures when restore or build operations fail with access errors.

**When to use this tool:**
- Build or restore operations fail with authentication errors for private NuGet feeds
- Error messages contain NU1301 (unable to load service index for source)
- HTTP 401 (Unauthorized) or 403 (Forbidden) errors when accessing NuGet feeds
- Errors mention "Unable to find package" from Azure DevOps feeds (pkgs.dev.azure.com)
- Package restore fails with "Unable to load the service index" from authenticated feeds

**How this tool works (requires human-in-the-loop):**
1. Invokes the Azure Artifacts credential provider in interactive mode
2. The credential provider outputs authentication instructions (typically a device code and URL)
3. User must manually open the provided URL in a browser and complete authentication
4. After user completes authentication, call this tool again to verify credentials are cached
5. Once credentials are verified, retry the failed operation

**Important:** This tool does NOT automatically open a browser. It provides instructions that the user must follow manually. After the user authenticates, you must call this tool again to verify the credentials are properly cached before retrying the build.

Extract the failing feed URL from error messages to use as the feedUrl parameter.

name: mcp_copilotmod_convert_project_to_sdk_style
description:
Call convert_project_to_sdk_style to convert the specified .NET project to an SDK-style project. Ensure that you discovered full absolute path to the project 
file before calling this tool (if you don't know the path, you can use get_solution_path tool to get solution file path and 
get_projects_info to get information for all projects in solution).
IMPORTANT: Do not call this tool for multiple projects in parallel. Wait for each conversion to complete before starting the next one. 
The underlying MSBuild infrastructure uses shared global state that is not safe for concurrent access.

name: mcp_copilotmod_discover_test_projects
description:
Call discover_test_projects to discover test projects.
Given an array of project paths, this function returns an array of strings containing the paths of all test projects.
If it returns null, it means the test service is unavailable.

name: mcp_copilotmod_get_instructions
description:
Adaptive instructions retrieval tool - behavior depends on parameters provided.

LIST mode (discovery):
  get_instructions(kind='skill')
    → Lists: available skills

  get_instructions(kind='scenario')
    → Lists all available scenarios

GET mode (retrieval with 'kind'):
  - kind='skill': Get skill by the ID provided in query parameter or search for skills using natural language search terms
    get_instructions(query='modernization-overview', kind='skill')

  - kind='scenario': Get scenario-specific requirements and guidance
    get_instructions(query='New-DotNet-Version', kind='scenario')

HELP mode:
  get_instructions()
    → Shows detailed usage guide

Valid kinds: scenario, skill

The tool automatically determines mode based on which parameters you provide.
Errors include helpful suggestions for correct usage.

name: mcp_copilotmod_get_solution_path
description: Call get_solution_path to get path of currently loaded solution.

name: mcp_copilotmod_open_dashboard
description:
Call open_dashboard to open the modernization dashboard for the current repository.
The dashboard shows upgrade scenario progress, assessment results, dependency health,
file changes, and build status in a web-based UI.
Returns the dashboard URL that can be opened in a browser.
If the dashboard is already running for this repository, returns the existing URL.

This is crucial for ensuring that the search quality remains high, especially after significant changes to the codebase or when the initial search results are unsatisfactory. 

Together, these tools create a robust ecosystem for codebase interaction, allowing developers to quickly access information, maintain an organized workspace, and enhance their productivity through effective search and retrieval functionalities.

Be sure to call this tool if you need a capability related to the above.

This group of tools is focused on managing comments related to pull requests and issues within GitHub repositories. The primary functionality includes adding comments to pending pull request reviews and specific issues. The tool 'mcp_github_add_comment_to_pending_review' allows users to provide feedback on the latest pending review, ensuring that reviewers can communicate effectively with the requesters. Meanwhile, 'mcp_github_add_issue_comment' enables users to comment on specific issues or pull requests, facilitating discussions and clarifications on ongoing work. Together, these tools enhance collaboration and communication among developers, making it easier to address concerns and provide insights during the code review process.

Be sure to call this tool if you need a capability related to the above.

name: activate_pull_request_management_tools
description:
Call this tool when you need access to a new category of tools. The category of tools is described as follows:

This collection of tools is designed for creating and managing pull requests in GitHub repositories. Users can create new branches, initiate pull requests, and even delegate tasks to GitHub Copilot for automated code implementation. The tools also allow for listing existing pull requests and merging them once they are approved. By providing functionalities for both creating and updating pull requests, as well as integrating with Copilot for code suggestions, this group enhances the workflow for developers working collaboratively on code changes.

Be sure to call this tool if you need a capability related to the above.

name: activate_github_repository_management_tools
description:
Call this tool when you need access to a new category of tools. The category of tools is described as follows:

This group encompasses a variety of tools designed for managing and retrieving information from GitHub repositories. The tools allow users to access detailed information about commits, files, labels, releases, and issues. For instance, 'mcp_github_get_commit' retrieves details about specific commits, while 'mcp_github_get_file_contents' allows users to view the contents of files or directories. Additionally, tools like 'mcp_github_list_issues' and 'mcp_github_issue_read' provide functionalities for listing and reading issues, which are crucial for tracking bugs and feature requests. The ability to create or update issues is facilitated by 'mcp_github_issue_write', ensuring that users can manage their project tasks effectively. Overall, these tools provide a comprehensive suite for developers to interact with and manage their GitHub repositories efficiently.

Be sure to call this tool if you need a capability related to the above.

name: activate_release_management_tools
description:
Call this tool when you need access to a new category of tools. The category of tools is described as follows:

This group focuses on managing releases within GitHub repositories. Users can retrieve specific releases by their tag names and list all available tags in a repository. name: mcp_todos_todo_write
description:
Use this tool to create and manage a structured task list for your current coding session. This helps you track progress, organize complex tasks, and demonstrate thoroughness to the user.

<when-to-use>
Use this tool proactively in these scenarios:
1. Complex multi-step tasks - When a task requires 3 or more distinct steps or actions
2. Non-trivial and complex tasks - Tasks that require careful planning or multiple operations
3. User explicitly requests todo list - When the user directly asks you to use the todo list
4. User provides multiple tasks - When users provide a list of things to be done
5. After receiving new instructions - Immediately capture user requirements as todos
6. When you start working on a task - Mark it as in_progress BEFORE beginning work
7. After completing a task - Mark it as completed and add any new follow-up tasks

Skip when:
• Single, straightforward task
• Task is trivial (< 3 steps)
• Purely conversational or informational
</when-to-use>

<persistence-reminder>
CRITICAL: Keep planning until the user's request is FULLY broken down. Do not stop at high-level tasks - decompose until each task is independently actionable (2-4 hour chunks).
</persistence-reminder>

<instructions>
  <threshold-rule>
  Use todos for ANY work requiring 3+ steps OR multiple contexts/files
  </threshold-rule>
  
  <task-categories>
  This tool tracks ALL work types:
  • Coding: features, bugs, refactoring, optimization, security
  • Research: codebase exploration, technology evaluation, root cause analysis
  • Documentation: API docs, guides, architecture docs, migration guides
  • Planning: system design, roadmaps, technical debt, process improvements
  • Learning: framework deep-dives, technology exploration, codebase onboarding
  </task-categories>

  <workflow-rules>
  ⚠️ PLAN FIRST: Never start work without todos for 3+ step tasks
  ⚠️ SINGLE PROGRESS: Only ONE task can be in_progress at any time
  ⚠️ IMMEDIATE UPDATES: Mark in_progress BEFORE starting, completed IMMEDIATELY when done
  ⚠️ COMPLETE FIRST: Finish current task before starting next
  ⚠️ DOCUMENT BLOCKERS: Keep tasks in_progress with ADR notes if blocked
  </workflow-rules>
  
  <status-transitions>
  • pending → in_progress: BEFORE starting work
  • in_progress → completed: IMMEDIATELY after finishing
  • Never leave tasks in_progress when switching
  </status-transitions>
</instructions>

<parameter-guidance>
  <todos>Complete array replacing entire todo list - include ALL existing incomplete todos</todos>
  <id>kebab-case verb-noun (e.g., "implement-auth", "fix-memory-leak")</id>
  <content>Specific, actionable description of what needs to be done</content>
  <status>pending/in_progress/completed - only ONE in_progress allowed</status>
  <priority>high (urgent/blocking), medium (important), low (nice-to-have)</priority>
  <adr>Architecture decisions, trade-offs, blockers, implementation notes</adr>
</parameter-guidance>

<critical-warning>
⚠️ This tool REPLACES the entire todo list - always include existing todos you want to keep
⚠️ Use todo_read first if uncertain about current todos
⚠️ Never lose existing work by forgetting to include current todos in the update
</critical-warning>

<success-pattern>
1. Read current todos (if any exist)
2. Analyze task complexity (3+ steps = use todos)
3. Plan new work by adding/updating tasks
4. Mark appropriate task as in_progress before coding
5. Update progress as you work
6. Mark completed when finished
</success-pattern>

<best-practices>
• Front-load research and investigation tasks
• Make each task independently verifiable
• Use subtasks for multi-day efforts
• Document assumptions and decisions in ADR
• Keep task descriptions specific and measurable
</best-practices>

description:
Apply automated code refactoring to Python files. Returns refactored content (does not modify original file) unless mode is "update". Use for: extracting functions, organizing Python imports, improving Python code structure, applying refactoring patterns.  Optional "mode" parameter: "update" updates the file, "edits" returns a WorkspaceEdit, "string" returns updated content as string. If mode is not specified, "update" will be used as the default. The "edits" mode is helpful for determining if a file needs changes (for example, to remove unused imports or fix import formatting) without making any modifications; if no changes are needed, the result will be either an empty WorkspaceEdit or a message indicating that no text edits were found. Available refactorings: source.unusedImports: - Removes all unused import statements from a Python file. Use when imports are imported but never referenced in the code. Requires fileUri parameter pointing to a Python file with unused imports.
source.convertImportFormat: - Converts import statements between absolute and relative formats according to python.analysis.importFormat setting. Use when import format consistency is needed. Requires fileUri parameter pointing to a Python file with imports to convert.
source.convertImportStar: - Converts all wildcard imports (from module import *) to explicit imports listing all imported symbols. Use when explicit imports are preferred for better code clarity and IDE support. Requires fileUri parameter pointing to a Python file with wildcard imports.
source.convertImportToModule: - Converts `from module import name1, name2` (including wildcard imports) into `import module` and rewrites references to `module.name1`, `module.name2`. Use when you want module-qualified references. Requires fileUri parameter pointing to a Python file with `from ... import ...` statements.
source.renameShadowedStdlibImports: - Renames imported user modules that shadow standard library module names (e.g. a local calendar.py). Use to avoid import shadowing bugs. Requires fileUri parameter pointing to the importing Python file.
source.addTypeAnnotation: - Adds type annotations to all variables and functions in a Python file that can be inferred from their usage. Use when type hints are needed for better type checking and code clarity. Requires fileUri parameter pointing to a Python file with unannotated variables or functions.
source.fixAll.pylance: - Applies all available automatic code fixes from python.analysis.fixAll setting. Use when multiple code issues need to be addressed simultaneously. Requires fileUri parameter pointing to a Python file with fixable issues.

This group of tools is focused on setting up the essential components for Java development. It includes tools for installing the Java Development Kit (JDK) and Apache Maven, both of which are critical for building and managing Java applications. The 'install_jdk' tool allows users to download and install a specific version of the JDK from trusted sources such as Microsoft or Eclipse Adoptium, ensuring that developers have the necessary environment to compile and run Java applications. The installation path is returned, making it easy to configure the development environment afterward.

The 'install_maven' tool complements the JDK installation by providing a way to install Apache Maven, a powerful build automation tool used primarily for Java projects. Maven simplifies the process of managing project dependencies, building projects, and deploying applications. Like the JDK installation, this tool downloads Maven from a trusted source and returns the installation path, facilitating seamless integration into the development workflow.

Together, these tools streamline the setup process for Java developers, allowing them to quickly establish a working environment with the correct versions of JDK and Maven. This is particularly useful when starting new projects or when specific versions are required that are not already installed on the system.

By using these tools in conjunction, developers can ensure that their Java projects are built on a solid foundation, with the right tools in place to manage dependencies and build processes efficiently. This group is essential for anyone looking to develop Java applications, whether they are beginners or experienced developers.

In summary, the 'java_development_tools' group provides a streamlined approach to setting up a Java development environment, ensuring that developers have the necessary tools to create, build, and manage their Java applications effectively.

Be sure to call this tool if you need a capability related to the above.

name: activate_infrastructure_best_practices_tools
description:
Call this tool when you need access to a new category of tools. The category of tools is described as follows:

This group focuses on ensuring that users adhere to best practices when creating Infrastructure as Code (IaC) for Azure deployments. The 'Get IaC rules' tool provides guidelines for developing Bicep and Terraform files, ensuring that users create high-quality, compatible configurations. Additionally, the 'Get WAF rules' tool offers insights into the Azure Well-Architected Framework, helping users implement secure and compliant configurations for their Azure resources. Together, these tools promote the development of robust and efficient infrastructure setups, reducing the risk of misconfigurations and enhancing the overall quality of Azure deployments.

Be sure to call this tool if you need a capability related to the above.

name: mcp_github_search_repositories
description: Find GitHub repositories by name, description, readme, topics, or other metadata. Perfect for discovering projects, finding examples, or locating specific repositories across GitHub.

name: mcp_github_search_code
description: Fast and precise code search across ALL GitHub repositories using GitHub's native search engine. Best for finding exact symbols, functions, classes, or specific code patterns.

name: activate_context_analysis_tools
description:
Call this tool when you need access to a new category of tools. The category of tools is described as follows:

This group of tools is designed for in-depth context analysis and memory retrieval within codebases. The tools facilitate lightweight context searches, session memory retrieval, and execution path tracing, allowing developers to quickly access relevant code and insights from previous sessions. The 'mcp_vexp_get_context_capsule' tool enables fast semantic and graph-based searches for relevant code snippets, making it ideal for quick lookups. In contrast, 'mcp_vexp_get_session_context' captures and retrieves observations from current and past sessions, providing a historical perspective on code exploration and decision-making.

Additionally, the 'mcp_vexp_search_logic_flow' tool is essential for understanding the flow of execution between code symbols, helping developers trace data and control paths, which is particularly useful for debugging and feature implementation analysis. The 'mcp_vexp_search_memory' tool enhances this capability by allowing users to search across all session memories using keywords and semantic similarity, ensuring that relevant past decisions and code paths are easily accessible.

Together, these tools create a robust framework for navigating and understanding complex codebases, enabling developers to make informed decisions based on historical context and execution paths. They are particularly useful during debugging sessions, feature development, and code refactoring, where understanding the implications of changes is critical.

Be sure to call this tool if you need a capability related to the above.

name: activate_code_inspection_tools
description:
Call this tool when you need access to a new category of tools. The category of tools is described as follows:

This group of tools focuses on efficient code inspection and analysis, providing developers with the means to explore and understand code structures without the overhead of raw content retrieval. The 'mcp_vexp_get_skeleton' tool is the preferred method for inspecting files, offering varying levels of detail on signatures, class declarations, and type definitions. This tool is designed to save tokens and streamline the inspection process, making it a go-to option for understanding the structure of functions and classes within a file.

The 'mcp_vexp_run_pipeline' tool serves as the primary tool for any codebase task, executing a comprehensive analysis pipeline that includes context search, impact analysis, and memory recall. This tool is crucial for preemptive analysis before code changes, debugging sessions, and refactoring efforts, as it provides a consolidated result that includes relevant source code and file skeletons while minimizing token usage.

By utilizing these tools together, developers can efficiently navigate and analyze codebases, ensuring they have the necessary context and insights before making changes. The combination of high-level file inspections and detailed analysis pipelines allows for a thorough understanding of code structures and their implications, ultimately leading to more effective coding practices and reduced errors.

Be sure to call this tool if you need a capability related to the above.

name: mcp_github_copilo_appmod-python-run-test
description: (For Python application migration only) This tool runs tests in the Python project and reports any detected errors or test failures after migration.

name: mcp_github_copilo_appmod-python-validate-lint
description: (For Python application migration only) This tool checks Python code linting issues and fix any detected linting issues after migration.

name: mcp_vexp_workspace_setup
description: Set up vexp for the current workspace. Generates configuration files, detects AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Continue), and provides setup instructions. Run this once when starting to work on a new project.

name: runTests
description: Runs unit tests in files. Use this tool if the user asks to run tests or when you want to validate changes using unit tests, and prefer using this tool instead of the terminal tool. When possible, always try to provide `files` paths containing the relevant unit tests in order to avoid unnecessarily long test runs. This tool outputs detailed information about the results of the test run. Set mode="coverage" to also collect coverage and optionally provide coverageFiles for focused reporting.

name: activate_java_project_build_and_testing_tools
description:
Call this tool when you need access to a new category of tools. The category of tools is described as follows:

This group of tools is designed to facilitate the development and testing of Java projects. The 'appmod-build-java-project' tool is essential for building Java applications using popular build systems like Maven or Gradle. It intelligently detects the appropriate build tool and JDK, allowing developers to quickly check the build status after making changes to the code or dependencies. This ensures that any build errors are identified early in the development process, promoting a smoother workflow.

Complementing the build tool, the 'appmod-generate-tests-for-java' tool automates the creation of test cases for Java classes within the project. By iterating through all Java classes, it generates relevant test cases, which can save developers significant time, especially in larger projects. This tool emphasizes the importance of testing in the software development lifecycle, ensuring that code changes do not introduce new bugs.

Finally, the 'appmod-run-tests-for-java' tool allows developers to execute the generated test cases using the same build tool, providing immediate feedback on test results. It reports any test errors or failures, enabling developers to address issues promptly. Together, these tools create a robust environment for building, testing, and maintaining Java applications, ensuring high-quality software delivery.

By using these tools in conjunction, developers can streamline their workflow from code changes to testing, thereby enhancing productivity and code quality. The integration of building and testing processes is crucial for continuous integration and deployment practices, making this group indispensable for Java developers.

Be sure to call this tool if you need a capability related to the above.

name: activate_java_upgrade_management_tools
description:
Call this tool when you need access to a new category of tools. The category of tools is described as follows:

This group of tools is focused on managing the upgrade process for Java projects, ensuring a smooth transition to newer versions or modernized frameworks. The 'appmod-confirm-upgrade-plan' tool plays a critical role in this process by presenting a generated upgrade plan to the user. It allows users to review and make adjustments to the plan before confirming it for execution, which is vital for ensuring that the upgrade aligns with project requirements and expectations.

The second tool, 'appmod-redirect-to-upgrade-agent', serves as the gateway to a specialized upgrade agent that handles the entire upgrade workflow. When invoked, it initiates a new chat session with the upgrade agent, passing along the user's upgrade request. This agent is equipped to guide users through the planning, execution, and verification stages of the upgrade process, providing expert assistance and ensuring that all necessary steps are followed.

Together, these tools create a comprehensive framework for managing Java project upgrades. The confirmation step ensures that users have control over the upgrade plan, while the redirection to the upgrade agent provides access to specialized knowledge and support. This combination minimizes the risks associated with upgrades, such as compatibility issues or loss of functionality.

By utilizing these tools, developers can confidently navigate the complexities of upgrading Java projects, ensuring that they remain up-to-date with the latest technologies and best practices. This group is essential for teams looking to modernize their Java applications while maintaining stability and performance.

Be sure to call this tool if you need a capability related to the above.

name: appmod-validate-cves-for-java
description: This tools checks if the given Java dependencies have any known vulnerabilities (CVEs). It will return a list of CVE issues found in the given dependencies, along with their severity and description. You MUST pass the dependencies to check as input, be careful that each dependency MUST be in the format of `groupId:artifactId:version`, e.g. `org.apache.commons:commons-lang3:3.12.0`. You must filter out any dependencies if you can not determine the version of them. You should use this tool to check for any known CVEs in the dependencies of the Java project

name: activate_python_environment_tools
description:
Call this tool when you need access to a new category of tools. The category of tools is described as follows:

This group of tools is designed to facilitate the management and retrieval of information regarding Python environments. The tools included are specifically tailored for Python environments such as conda, venv, and other virtual environment managers. They provide essential functionalities that help developers understand the configuration and setup of their Python environments, which is crucial for ensuring compatibility and proper execution of Python scripts and applications.

The first tool, 'get_python_environment_details', retrieves comprehensive details about the specified Python environment. This includes the type of environment (e.g., conda or venv), the version of Python being used, and a list of all installed packages along with their respective versions. This information is vital for developers to ensure that they are working within the correct environment and that all necessary dependencies are installed.

The second tool, 'get_python_executable_details', focuses on providing the necessary details to construct the fully qualified path to the Python executable. It helps developers avoid common pitfalls associated with executing Python commands directly in the terminal by offering a structured way to run Python scripts or commands within the context of the specified environment. This ensures that the correct version of Python and the appropriate environment settings are utilized.

Together, these tools streamline the process of managing Python environments, making it easier for developers to configure their setups accurately and efficiently. By using these tools in conjunction, developers can quickly gather the necessary information about their environments and execute Python commands with confidence, reducing the likelihood of errors related to environment misconfiguration.

Overall, this group of tools is essential for any Python developer looking to maintain a clean and functional development environment, ensuring that their projects run smoothly and are supported by the correct dependencies.

Be sure to call this tool if you need a capability related to the above.

name: mcp_github_copilo2_typescript_write_upgrade_summary
description: Writes a short summary of the upgrade process to a file: how long the total upgrade took, how many packages were available to upgrade, and how many were successfully upgraded or not. Returns the summary in case it would be helpful to display.

name: mcp_github_copilo3_appmod-generate-k8s-manifest
description: Gather insights from knowledgebase and return requirements for Kubernetes/Helm/ACA/Kustomize manifest creation. Supports repository analysis or ACA manifest conversion.

name: mcp_github_copilo3_appmod-analyze-repository
description: Analyze repository structure and detect technologies by parsing config files to prepare for containerization and generating container artifacts like Dockerfiles and Kubernetes manifests

name: mcp_github_copilo3_appmod-get-iac-rules
description: This tool offers guidelines for creating Bicep/Terraform files to deploy applications on Azure as well as general Azure Resource Rules. The guidelines outline rules to improve the quality of Infrastructure as Code files and resource configurations, ensuring they are compatible with the azd tool or az cli and adhere to best practices.

name: mcp_github_copilo2_typescript_scan_dependencies
description: Scans a TypeScript project for outdated npm dependencies and returns structured JSON with dependency groups, monorepo info, TypeScript migration status, and feature flags. Use this to plan an upgrade before making changes.

name: mcp_copilotmod_get_projects_in_topological_order
description: Call get_projects_in_topological_order to retrieve a list of projects in topological order based on project dependencies.

name: mcp_github_copilo3_appmod-get-plan
description: Entry point to help the agent deploy a service to the cloud. Agent should read its output and generate a deploy plan in '.azure/plan.copilotmd' for execution steps, recommended Azure services based on the information agent detected from project. Before calling this tool, scan this workspace to detect the services to deploy and their dependent services. If user has existing resources and only wants to deploy to existing resources, agent MUST first ask user to provide EXISTING Azure resources' ARM IDs or pick the IDs if user wants to use Az CLI command! Do NOT run az login before calling this tool, even if terminal shows login errors.

name: mcp_github_copilo3_appmod-generate-architecture-diagram
description: Generates an azure service architecture diagram for the application. Call this tool when the user needs design or display of the azure architecture of their application. Before calling this tool, please scan this workspace to detect the services to deploy and their dependent services. If user uses existing resources for deployment, try to match the service type and names to the existing infrastructure. Try your best to fulfill the input schema with your analyze result.

name: mcp_github_copilo3_appmod-get-waf-rules
description: This tool provides Azure Well-Architected Framework (WAF) rules for Azure resources in Azure Application Landing Zone, ensuring secure, compliant, and production-ready configurations.

name: mcp_copilotmod_start_task
description:
Call start_task to start execution of a task in the workflow.
Sets the task status to "in_progress" and records the start time.
Must be called before making changes for a task.

name: mcp_copilotmod_initialize_scenario
description:
Call initialize_scenario to start a new modernization scenario.
Creates the scenario folder structure in .github/upgrades/<scenarioId>/<operationId>/ and initializes state.
Returns paths to scenario artifacts (assessment.md, plan.md, tasks.md, scenario-instructions.md).

name: mcp_github_copilo2_typescript_start_dev_server
description: Starts the project's dev server (npm run dev/start/serve) in the background. Waits for the server to be ready and returns the URL. Call typescript_stop_dev_server when done with runtime validation.

name: mcp_github_copilo3_appmod-get-azure-landing-zone-plan
description: Entry point to generate an IaC plan for a customized Azure Application Landing Zone. Use it to create tailored Azure Landing Zones that adhere to best practices and organizational standards.

name: mcp_github_copilo_appmod-recommend-migration-tasks
description: This is the start point for "Migrate to Azure" for Java applications. Every time a user wants to "Migrate to Azure", "migrate my Java app to Azure", "move to Azure", or any Azure migration for a Java application, call this tool immediately as the first and primary action. Do not attempt to analyze the codebase yourself. Do not call other migration tools directly. This tool identifies the appropriate Azure migration tasks for the workspace. If an AppCAT assessment report exists, recommendations are derived directly from the report. Otherwise, it analyzes the workspace using file pattern matching to detect technologies and suggest appropriate migration tasks. After receiving recommendations, present the options to the user for selection before proceeding.

name: mcp_github_issue_read
description: Get information about a specific issue in a GitHub repository.

name: get_changed_files
description: Get git diffs of current file changes in a git repository. Don't forget that you can use run_in_terminal to run git commands in a terminal as well.

name: get_errors
description: Get any compile or lint errors in a specific file or across all files. If the user mentions errors or problems in a file, they may be referring to these. Use the tool to see the same errors that the user is seeing. If the user asks you to analyze all errors, or does not specify a file, use this tool to gather errors for all files. Also use this tool after editing a file to validate the change.

name: copilot_getNotebookSummary
description: This is a tool returns the list of the Notebook cells along with the id, cell types, line ranges, language, execution information and output mime types for each cell. This is useful to get Cell Ids when executing a notebook or determine what cells have been executed and what order, or what cells have outputs. If required to read contents of a cell use this to determine the line range of a cells, and then use read_file tool to read a specific line range. Requery this tool if the contents of the notebook change.

name: read_notebook_cell_output
description: This tool will retrieve the output for a notebook cell from its most recent execution or restored from disk. The cell may have output even when it has not been run in the current kernel session. This tool has a higher token limit for output length than the runNotebookCell tool.

name: vscode_askQuestions
description: Use this tool to ask the user a small number of clarifying questions before proceeding. Provide the questions array with concise headers and prompts. Use options for fixed choices, set multiSelect when multiple selections are allowed. Users can always provide a freeform text answer alongside options unless you set allowFreeformInput to false.

name: terminal_last_command
description: Get the last command run in the active terminal.

name: terminal_selection
description: Get the current selection in the active terminal.

name: mcp_github_copilo3_appmod-get-cicd-pipeline-guidance
description: This tool helps create a CI/CD pipeline to deploy a project to Azure. BEFORE calling this tool, you MUST confirm with user 1. if they want to use Github Actions/ADO pipeline/GitLab CICD 2. if they have existing Azure resources to deploy for different environments. If user has existing Azure resources, *ASK* for subscription ID, resource groups, environments, Azure hosting service TYPEs. If user does not have existing resources, *ASK* whether to include provision in the pipeline. *DO NOT call this tool UNTIL you made these confirmations with user*.

name: mcp_github_copilo3_appmod-diagnostic-existing-resources
description: This tool analyzes existing Azure resources to diagnose their configurations and connections, and provides recommendations to prevent application deployment failures. Use this tool when the user has Azure existing resources and wants to deploy new applications that depend on those resources. Note it can only diagnose configuration of Container Apps and AKS to access ACR.

name: create_new_jupyter_notebook
description: Generates a new Jupyter Notebook (.ipynb) in VS Code. Jupyter Notebooks are interactive documents commonly used for data exploration, analysis, visualization, and combining code with narrative text. Prefer creating plain Python files or similar unless a user explicitly requests creating a new Jupyter Notebook or already has a Jupyter Notebook opened or exists in the workspace.

name: create_new_workspace
description:
Get comprehensive setup steps to help the user create complete project structures in a VS Code workspace. This tool is designed for full project initialization and scaffolding, not for creating individual files.

When to use this tool:
- User wants to create a new complete project from scratch
- Setting up entire project frameworks (TypeScript projects, React apps, Node.js servers, etc.)
- Initializing Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers with full structure
- Creating VS Code extensions with proper scaffolding
- Setting up Next.js, Vite, or other framework-based projects
- User asks for "new project", "create a workspace", "set up a [framework] project"
- Need to establish complete development environment with dependencies, config files, and folder structure

When NOT to use this tool:
- Creating single files or small code snippets
- Adding individual files to existing projects
- Making modifications to existing codebases
- User asks to "create a file" or "add a component"
- Simple code examples or demonstrations
- Debugging or fixing existing code

This tool provides complete project setup including:
- Folder structure creation
- Package.json and dependency management
- Configuration files (tsconfig, eslint, etc.)
- Initial boilerplate code
- Development environment setup
- Build and run instructions

Use other file creation tools for individual files within existing projects.

name: edit_notebook_file
description:
This is a tool for editing an existing Notebook file in the workspace. Generate the "explanation" property first.
The system is very smart and can understand how to apply your edits to the notebooks.
When updating the content of an existing cell, ensure newCode preserves whitespace and indentation exactly and does NOT include any code markers such as (...existing code...).

name: get_vscode_api
description:
Get comprehensive VS Code API documentation and references for extension development. This tool provides authoritative documentation for VS Code's extensive API surface, including proposed APIs, contribution points, and best practices. Use this tool for understanding complex VS Code API interactions.

When to use this tool:
- User asks about specific VS Code APIs, interfaces, or extension capabilities
- Need documentation for VS Code extension contribution points (commands, views, settings, etc.)
- Questions about proposed APIs and their usage patterns
- Understanding VS Code extension lifecycle, activation events, and packaging
- Best practices for VS Code extension development architecture
- API examples and code patterns for extension features
- Troubleshooting extension-specific issues or API limitations

When NOT to use this tool:
- Creating simple standalone files or scripts unrelated to VS Code extensions
- General programming questions not specific to VS Code extension development
- Questions about using VS Code as an editor (user-facing features)
- Non-extension related development tasks
- File creation or editing that doesn't involve VS Code extension APIs

CRITICAL usage guidelines:
1. Always include specific API names, interfaces, or concepts in your query
2. Mention the extension feature you're trying to implement
3. Include context about proposed vs stable APIs when relevant
4. Reference specific contribution points when asking about extension manifest
5. Be specific about the VS Code version or API version when known

Scope: This tool is for EXTENSION DEVELOPMENT ONLY - building tools that extend VS Code itself, not for general file creation or non-extension programming tasks.

name: run_notebook_cell
description: This is a tool for running a code cell in a notebook file directly in the notebook editor. The output from the execution will be returned. Code cells should be run as they are added or edited when working through a problem to bring the kernel state up to date and ensure the code executes successfully. Code cells are ready to run and don't require any pre-processing. If asked to run the first cell in a notebook, you should run the first code cell since markdown cells cannot be executed. NOTE: Avoid executing Markdown cells or providing Markdown cell IDs, as Markdown cells cannot be  executed.

name: run_vscode_command
description: Run a command in VS Code. Use this tool to run a command in Visual Studio Code as part of a new workspace creation process only.

name: switch_agent
description:
Switch to the Plan agent to align on approach before implementing. Plan will explore the codebase, gathers context, clarifies requirements with the user, and creates an actionable implementation plan.

SWITCH TO PLAN when ANY of these apply:
1. Adding new functionality - where should it go? What patterns to follow?
2. Multiple valid approaches exist - choosing between technologies, patterns, or strategies
3. Modifying existing behavior - unclear what should change or what side effects exist
4. Architectural decisions required - choosing between design patterns or integration approaches
5. Changes span multiple files - refactoring, migrations, or cross-cutting concerns
6. Requirements are underspecified - need to explore before understanding scope

EXAMPLES:
✓ Switch to Plan:
- "Add authentication to the app" → architectural decisions needed (session vs JWT, middleware)
- "Refactor this data flow" → must understand component dependencies first
- "Migrate from X to Y" → requires understanding current structure

✗ Do NOT switch to Plan:
- User attached a detailed spec, plan, or requirements doc → context already provided
- You already started editing files in this conversation → too late to switch
- Single obvious change like fixing a typo or renaming → just do it
- User gave explicit step-by-step instructions → follow them directly

name: create_and_run_task
description: Creates and runs a build, run, or custom task for the workspace by generating or adding to a tasks.json file based on the project structure (such as package.json or README.md). If the user asks to build, run, launch and they have no tasks.json file, use this tool. If they ask to create or add a task, use this tool.

name: mcp_copilotmod_get_dotnet_upgrade_options
description:
Call get_dotnet_upgrade_options to get options and default parameters for upgrading .NET projects to a newer .NET version.
This tool is specific to the **dotnet-version-upgrade** and **azure-functions-upgrade** scenarios. Do NOT call it outside those scenarios.
It returns:
- Solution and project file paths
- Proposed .NET version to upgrade to
- Available target frameworks the project can be upgraded to (with support level and end-of-life dates)

Also use this tool when the user asks which .NET versions a project can be upgraded to.

name: mcp_copilotmod_get_member_info
description:
Call get_member_info to get detailed information about .NET type or interface member (method, property, field etc) used in the specified project. Information can contain 
- full type name,
- the package or assembly where type is defined,
- if package was updated, list of new type members that could be used instead of the old one,
- potential breaking changes associated with the updated type member,
- other public members defined in the type.
- any additional metadata associated with the member.
- any other relevant information that helps in understanding the member's context.

name: mcp_copilotmod_get_namespace_info
description:
Call get_namespace_info to get detailed information about .NET namespace used in the specified project. Information can contain 
- the package or assembly where namespace is defined,
- if package was updated, list of new namespaces that could be used instead of the old ones,
- potential breaking changes associated with the updated namespaces,
- public types defined in the namespace.

name: mcp_copilotmod_get_project_dependencies
description:
Call get_project_dependencies to get detailed dependencies information for specified project. It returns a list of project dependencies (packages, 
assemblies, frameworks, projects) and imported targets with their metadata including names, versions and definition paths (dependencies 
could be defined in the project file or in targets imported by the project).

name: mcp_copilotmod_get_scenarios
description: Call get_scenarios to get available modernization scenarios. It returns a list of ID and short description for each scenario.

name: mcp_copilotmod_get_supported_package_version
description: Call get_supported_package_version to retrieve the latest supported version of a specified package for a given project file. It returns the version information along with any relevant issues found during the retrieval process.

name: mcp_copilotmod_get_type_info
description:
Call get_type_info to get detailed information about .NET type (class, struct, record, interface etc) used in the specified project. Information can contain 
- full type name,
- the package or assembly where type is defined,
- if package was updated, list of new types that could be used instead of the old ones,
- potential breaking changes associated with the updated type,
- public members defined in the type.

name: mcp_copilotmod_resume_scenario
description:
Call resume_scenario to resume an existing scenario that was discovered on disk.
Use this when get_state reports existing scenarios and the user wants to continue one.
Associates the existing scenario with the current session without creating a new one.

name: mcp_github_add_comment_to_pending_review
description: Add review comment to the requester's latest pending pull request review. A pending review needs to already exist to call this (check with the user if not sure).

name: mcp_github_add_issue_comment
description: Add a comment to a specific issue in a GitHub repository. Use this tool to add comments to pull requests as well (in this case pass pull request number as issue_number), but only if user is not asking specifically to add review comments.

name: mcp_github_add_reply_to_pull_request_comment
description: Add a reply to an existing pull request comment. This creates a new comment that is linked as a reply to the specified comment.

name: mcp_github_copilo_appmod-dotnet-build-project
description: (For .NET application migration only) This tool uses dotnet CLI to build your .NET project or solution and report any detected errors. Use this tool to verify your .NET code after making changes and fix any build errors found.

name: mcp_github_copilo_appmod-python-check-type
description: (For Python application migration only) This tool performs type checking on the specified Python files within a given workspace. It analyzes the code for type-related issues, ensuring that type annotations and usages are consistent and correct according to Python typing standards. The tool generates a report of any type errors or warnings found during the analysis, helping developers identify and resolve potential type-related problems in their codebase.

name: mcp_github_copilo_appmod-python-coordinate-validation-stage
description: (For Python application migration only) This tool coordinates the iterative validation stages during the Python code migration process. It delegates specific validation tasks to specialized subagents for each stage, collects their results, and determines the overall progress of the migration. The coordinator ensures that each validation stage is executed in sequence, tracks iterations and attempts, and provides structured feedback to guide further migration efforts.

name: mcp_github_copilo_appmod-python-validate-syntax
description: (For Python application migration only) This tool checks Python code syntax and fix any detected syntax errors after migration.

name: mcp_github_copilo2_typescript_compile_package
description: Compile a package using tsc, the typescript compiler.

name: mcp_github_copilo2_typescript_install_dependencies
description: Install dependencies for a project using the appropriate package manager.

name: mcp_github_copilo2_typescript_report_telemetry
description: Reports telemetry for TypeScript upgrade workflow events that are not already tracked by other tools. Use this for TypeScript migration completions, runtime validation results, and test generation outcomes.

name: mcp_github_copilo2_typescript_run_tests
description: Run tests for a project using the test specified in package.json.

name: mcp_github_copilo2_typescript_stop_dev_server
description: Stops the dev server that was started by typescript_start_dev_server.

name: mcp_github_copilo2_typescript_upgrade_package_dependency_group
description: Upgrade a group of dependencies in the given TypeScript project.

name: mcp_github_copilo2_typescript_verify_upgrade
description: Verify the build state after you have applied fixes to resolve errors reported by typescript_upgrade_package_dependency_group. Optionally accepts regex-based fixes to apply before verifying. Builds the project and compares errors against the baseline. Returns 'complete' if all errors are resolved, 'needs_client_fixes' with remaining errors if more work is needed, or 'failed' if no progress is being made (stall detection) or the maximum number of rounds is reached.

name: mcp_pylance_mcp_s_pylanceLSP
description:
Read-only Language Server Protocol access for Python. Exposes 31 LSP methods for code intelligence. Parameters and responses follow the LSP specification. Use method "help" for full documentation of all 31 methods including parameters, responses, and usage guidance.

## Core Methods (quick reference)

### textDocument/hover
Get hover information (type info, docstrings) at a position.
Params: { textDocument: { uri }, position: { line, character } }
Response: { contents: MarkupContent, range?: Range } | null

### textDocument/completion
Get completion items at a position. Returns core completions (no auto-imports).
Params: { textDocument: { uri }, position: { line, character }, context?: { triggerCharacter?: string } }
Response: { isIncomplete: boolean, items: CompletionItem[] } | null

### completionItem/resolve
Resolve additional detail for a completion item returned by textDocument/completion.
Params: CompletionItem (as returned by textDocument/completion)
Response: CompletionItem (with documentation and additionalTextEdits filled in)

### textDocument/definition
Go to definition of the symbol at position.
Params: { textDocument: { uri }, position: { line, character } }
Response: Location[] | null — each Location: { uri, range }

### textDocument/references
Find all references to the symbol at position.
Params: { textDocument: { uri }, position: { line, character }, context?: { includeDeclaration?: boolean } }
Response: Location[] | null

### textDocument/documentSymbol
Get all symbols in a document (classes, functions, variables) as a hierarchical tree.
Params: { textDocument: { uri } }
Response: DocumentSymbol[] — each has name, kind, range, selectionRange, children?

### workspace/symbol
Search for symbols across the workspace by name.
Params: { query: string }
Response: SymbolInformation[] — each has name, kind, location: { uri, range }

### textDocument/signatureHelp
Get signature help (parameter info) at a call site.
Params: { textDocument: { uri }, position: { line, character } }
Response: { signatures: SignatureInformation[], activeSignature?, activeParameter? } | null

### textDocument/diagnostic
Get diagnostics (errors, warnings) for a document.
Params: { textDocument: { uri } }
Response: { kind: "full", items: Diagnostic[] } — each Diagnostic: { range, message, severity }

### callHierarchy/prepare
Find the callable symbol at position (first step for incoming/outgoing call analysis).
Params: { textDocument: { uri }, position: { line, character } }
Response: CallHierarchyItem[] | null

## Parameter Conventions
- uri: File URI string, e.g. "file:///path/to/file.py"
- position: { line: number, character: number } — both 0-based
- range: { start: Position, end: Position }

Other methods: typeDefinition, declaration, implementation, documentHighlight, codeLens, foldingRange, selectionRange, inlayHint, semanticTokens, documentColor, colorPresentation, inlineValue, typeHierarchy, callHierarchy (incoming/outgoing). Use "help" for details on these.
